title: The Jews' rejection and Christ's service
english: He will establish their knowledge and their unbelief will be set right; for such are most especially the Jews, as if fleeing to other gods as an insult to God, and as if insulting God as not willing or not able to help, they ran to gods, trusting more in the help from others. For indeed they compelled Aaron to make gods for themselves which would go before them, as an insult and a reproach to God. Therefore, as concerning the person of Christ toward the Father, the psalm is said, saying: 'the insults of those insulting you have fallen upon me' (Psalm 88:50). From the presence of Christ, neither did the Jews still worship idols, and the nations were turned toward piety. The Lord has become a servant of the promise and of the philanthropy of God (Rom 15:8).
